records.original_predicate_paraphrase: With Mercury as reference, Sun third, Venus fourth, all remaining relevant classical planets fifth, and none debilitated or in enemies' signs: the verse associates the configuration with political rule.
records.original_source_short: रविस्तृतीयो भृगुनन्दन: सुखे बुधस्य चान्ये यदि पञ्चमे स्थिताः
records.astronomical_inference_separate: Under inclusive whole-sign counting third from Mercury means Sun/Mercury longitude bins two signs apart, minimum 30°, exceeding Mercury's approximate 28° maximum solar elongation. Therefore the stated third-from-Mercury antecedent is impossible in that model.
records.scope_limit: Other source meanings of bhava vs exact longitude/house not established; no real-world outcome or birth chart evaluated.

records.english_literal: Moon in own sign; Mercury Jupiter Saturn in fourth and own Navamsas, described as aspected by Sun.
records.sanskrit_supported_reading: Moon own sign and bright; Mercury Jupiter Venus (dānava-ijya = Venus) in own subdivisions in fourth, and aspected by Sun.
records.sanskrit_short: स्वांशे स्थिता बुधबृहस्पतिदानवेज्याः । पातालगा दिनकरेण निरीक्षिताश्च
records.source_discrepancy: English Sani/Saturn versus Sanskrit dānava-ijya (Venus), materially changes the predicted planet set.
records.astronomical_inference_separate: Under Sārāvalī Ch4.32–33 sign-aspect convention, Sun casts its minimum specified aspect to the third (2 signs offset), at least 30° from Sun's sign. Mercury is always within roughly 28° of Sun, so Mercury cannot receive any of those sign-defined solar aspects, including the stated fourth-house aspect, if the verse applies that same convention.
records.scope_limit: The verse's aspect modality and planetary-house convention must be frozen before a universal impossibility claim; does not prove that an independently specified alternate aspect calculation is empty.
